domainContext.summary: This is not a standard architectural Revit workflow. Families are repurposed Revit categories used to model precast concrete products, connections, and consumable materials. Understanding this mapping is essential for correct tool usage and future tool design.

assemblyMembershipTracking.method1_revitAPI: AssemblyInstance.GetMemberIds() — returns direct assembly members only (column + connection instance), NOT nested SE within connection
assemblyMembershipTracking.method2_assemblyNameParam: Assembly Name parameter on each member element matches assembly mark — e.g. column has Assembly Name = 'CLA017'
assemblyMembershipTracking.method3_productHostParams: CONSTRUCTION_PRODUCT_HOST and BOM_PRODUCT_HOST on placed instances — project-level shared parameters from template, NOT family parameters. Set to host product CONTROL_MARK (e.g. 'CLA017'). Used by custom tools for BOM traversal.
assemblyMembershipTracking.traversalDepth: Full BOM requires 3-level traversal: Assembly → Connection members → Nested SE within connection (plate assemblies) → Raw materials within plate assemblies

keyProductParameters.CONTROL_MARK: Piece mark — instance, shared, formula-driven on P*** and rebar families (changes with finish or bar end type)
keyProductParameters.CONTROL_NUMBER: Unique production number — separate from piece mark
keyProductParameters.ASSEMBLY_MARK_NUMBER: Assembly-level piece mark on the Assembly element itself
keyProductParameters.IDENTITY_DESCRIPTION: Full fabrication spec string — what the shop reads. Formula-driven on most families. Multi-line on complex assemblies.
keyProductParameters.IDENTITY_DESCRIPTION_SHORT: Abbreviated callout mark. Formula-driven. Used in schedule filters and tags.
keyProductParameters.MANUFACTURE_COMPONENT: Primary BOM classification key. Formula-driven on rebar and some SE. Determines BOM level and schedule filter membership.
keyProductParameters.ASSEMBLY_COMPONENT: Boolean flag (Yes/No). When 1, element is a scheduled assembly component nested in a plate assembly. Default 0 on standalone elements.
keyProductParameters.COMPONENT_WEIGHT: Piece weight. Formula-driven on rebar: (DIM_LENGTH / 1ft) × Component_Weight_Unit. Fixed value on plate assemblies.
keyProductParameters.SORTING_ORDER: BOM line item sequence. Formula-driven on rebar based on BAR_TYPE and ASSEMBLY_COMPONENT flags.
keyProductParameters.CONSTRUCTION_PRODUCT_HOST: Project parameter (not family). Links BOM element back to host product CONTROL_MARK.
keyProductParameters.BOM_PRODUCT_HOST: Project parameter (not family). Same linking function as CONSTRUCTION_PRODUCT_HOST for BOM tools.
keyProductParameters.COMMENTS: Used in schedule filters for ad-hoc classification — treat as structured data, not throwaway annotation.

manufactureComponentTaxonomy.EMBED STANDARD: P*** plate assembly level — BOM at plate level stops here
manufactureComponentTaxonomy.REBAR CUSTOM ASSEMBLY COMPONENT CIP RAW: CIP rebar nested in plate assembly
manufactureComponentTaxonomy.REBAR CUSTOM ASSEMBLY COMPONENT ERECTION: Erection rebar nested in plate assembly
manufactureComponentTaxonomy.note: RAW CONSUMABLE suffix marks purchasable/consumed materials. Same rebar family (e.g. S08) resolves to different MANUFACTURE_COMPONENT values based on BAR_TYPE_* instance flags — do NOT filter on family name alone.

rebarFamilyArchitecture.description: A single rebar family (e.g. S08 = #8 bar) handles all use contexts via boolean instance flags. MANUFACTURE_COMPONENT, SORTING_ORDER, CONTROL_MARK, IDENTITY_DESCRIPTION, and IDENTITY_DESCRIPTION_SHORT all resolve from these flags.
rebarFamilyArchitecture.assemblyFlag: ASSEMBLY_COMPONENT — when 1, bar is nested in a plate assembly. Overrides BAR_TYPE in SORTING_ORDER and MANUFACTURE_COMPONENT.
rebarFamilyArchitecture.taperFlags: TAPER_END1, TAPER_END2 — Lenton tapered thread ends. Shift IDENTITY_DESCRIPTION to call out coupler spec. CONTROL_MARK becomes 'Mark# Req'd' requiring unique piece mark assignment.
rebarFamilyArchitecture.weightFormula: (DIM_LENGTH / 1ft) × Component_Weight_Unit — live calculated, self-weighing at any length
rebarFamilyArchitecture.BAR_SHAPE: Type parameter — 'STRAIGHT' for S08. Bent bars have different family names with shape codes.
rebarFamilyArchitecture.namingConvention: S## = Straight bar, bar size number. e.g. S08 = #8 straight. Bent bars use shape prefix codes.

bomLevelStrategy.plateLevel: Filter MANUFACTURE_COMPONENT = 'EMBED STANDARD' — returns P*** assemblies as units. Plant knows BOM of each P***.
bomLevelStrategy.materialsLevel: Filter MANUFACTURE_COMPONENT CONTAINS 'RAW CONSUMABLE' — returns individual plates, rebar, bolts etc.
bomLevelStrategy.critical: NEVER query both levels simultaneously for the same product — shared nested families surface at all levels, causing double-counts.
bomLevelStrategy.scheduleTemplates: Will be covered later. Use compound parameter filters: MANUFACTURE_COMPONENT + ASSEMBLY_COMPONENT + BAR_TYPE_* + COMMENTS as needed.

finishSystem.formula: finish_check integer resolves to 0-5 via if-chain, drives CONTROL_MARK, IDENTITY_DESCRIPTION, MANUFACTURER_PLANT_ID, MANUFACTURER_PLANT_DESCRIPTION
finishSystem.note: CONTROL_MARK on P*** families is not static — always read the resolved value, never assume it equals the family name.

OST_StructuralFraming.role: Primary precast product families — ALL major concrete elements
OST_StructuralFraming.placementTool: create_beam (uses Revit Structural Framing placement API)
OST_StructuralFraming.notes: Despite the category name, these are not limited to steel beams. Every major precast product is modeled as Structural Framing. create_beam is the primary product placement tool.

OST_StructConnections.role: Hosting families for nested Specialty Equipment — connection containers
OST_StructConnections.placementType: FaceBased + WorkPlaneBased — placed on a face of the host product element
OST_StructConnections.notes: Container family. Carries nested SE families (plate assemblies, hardware), void families (bolt pockets), and grout families. MANUFACTURE_COMPONENT = 'CONNECTION'.

OST_SpecialtyEquipment.notes: Can host other Specialty Equipment to build up a part. Often loaded into Structural Connection families. Specialty Equipment nested in Specialty Equipment is a valid and common pattern.

OST_GenericModel.role: Void families and miscellaneous addon elements
examples: Addon geometry not fitting other categories
OST_GenericModel.notes: Primarily used for geometry subtraction and specialty add-ons.

OST_Walls.role: Finish and veneer tracking skins for precast panels
OST_Walls.notes: Custom wall families applied as skins over Structural Framing elements. Used to capture finish square footages and callout veneer/formliner patterns for specifications and schedules.

assemblyWorkflow.description: Assemblies are NOT created at the individual part level. Parts are built up by nesting Specialty Equipment into Structural Connections. Assemblies are only created at the project level to associate all elements that intersect face normals or lie interior to a Structural Framing element.
assemblyWorkflow.implication: Assembly creation tools are a future group but are project-level operations, not family-level.

sheetTypes.cdSheets: Regular Revit sheets — used for Contract Documents and plate drawings
sheetTypes.shopTickets: Assembly Sheets — used for shop drawing/fabrication tickets. Distinct from regular sheets in Revit and may require separate create_sheet handling.

domainContext.annotationUsage: Standard Revit annotation families, dimension families, and tags are used normally alongside the custom product families.
domainContext.toolPriorityImplication: Tool development should prioritize: OST_StructuralFraming placement and management (create_beam, get_family_placement_info), OST_SpecialtyEquipment hosted placement, OST_StructuralConnections as host containers, and query tools that filter by these categories. Generic architectural categories (doors, windows, furniture) are low priority.

designDecisions.dataFlow: C# reads instances.json (+ sibling datasets) from disk; only summary crosses MCP; per-element report + remap JSON written to disk.
designDecisions.passClassification: ClassifyPass: placement==null -> 0 (floors, skip). curve -> pass1. point: level-hosted (hostElementId in levels_grids OR workPlaneName startswith 'Level :' OR no host) -> pass1; else instance-hosted -> pass2.
designDecisions.datasetFinding: ALL 3247 SF + ALL 2583 GM records are WorkPlaneBased points; NO curve records in this model. Floor = 1 element (elementId 10080471), skipped by this tool (Part B.6).
designDecisions.levelResolution: target level by name: levelName ?? param 'Level' ?? param 'Schedule Level' ?? levels_grids[hostElementId] ?? ResolveClosestLevel(point.z). Names match template (LEVEL 1, ROOF, etc.).
designDecisions.placement: pass1 point: NewFamilyInstance(absolutePoint mm->ft, symbol, level, NonStructural); rotate rotationDeg about Z; flipFacing/flipHand per flags (guarded by CanFlip*). Placing at absolute z reproduces Offset-from-Host implicitly (offset param NOT written).
designDecisions.pass2: resolve host via hostGuidDecodedId ?? hostElementId through remap; cross-check hostFace.workPlaneName vs resolved host 'Family : Type' (mismatch => flag, DO NOT place). Face refs don't cross docs & facePoint/Normal are null here (work-plane hosted) => point fallback + hostVoidCutFlag (void auto-cut UNCONFIRMED -> Part B.4 pilot; may need InstanceVoidCutUtils v20.1).
designDecisions.orientation: rotationDeg + flips applied; residual (facing angle) + mirror mismatch recorded ONLY when maxElements<=64 (pilot; per-element regen). Bulk runs skip live verify for speed. mirrored NOT reproduced geometrically in v20 (flags only) — pilot will confirm sufficiency.
designDecisions.paramWrites_F1: GUID-keyed. shared params: for each source param name -> inventory GUIDs -> target.get_Parameter(guid); non-shared: LookupParameter(name). IsReadOnly skips formula/computed/builtins. raw authoritative: Length mm->ft, Angle deg->rad, other doubles as-is (internal). ElementId params skipped+reported. NOTE export BuildParameterMap dedups by NAME so only ONE value survives per duplicate name (DAP x3 etc.) — all GUID slots of a name get that single exported value (best available).
designDecisions.typeResolution: 1) exact (family+type) vs loaded symbols; 2) typemap entry -> loaded target OR (execute) load tgtFamilyFile + clone type from sibling, apply family_types[srcTypeId] params then typeParamOverrides; 3) unresolved (dryrun lists w/ counts, execute skips+logs).
designDecisions.chunking: one Transaction per 500 placements, progressively committed (lose at most one chunk on fatal). Soft deadline 540s -> return resumable partial. resumeFromIndex + nextIndex/done drive resume. Remap file rewritten (union) after each chunk commit.

patchQueue.title: New tool: get_family_placement_info
patchQueue.description: A pre-flight tool that takes a familyTypeId and returns: category name, FamilyPlacementType (OneLevelBased, WorkPlaneBased, FaceBased, TwoLevelBased, etc.), required host category if face-based, and valid view types for placement. Critical for the Metromont workflow where OST_StructuralFraming, OST_SpecialtyEquipment, OST_StructuralConnections, and OST_GenericModel each have different placement rules and hosting requirements. Enables AI to validate prerequisites and select the correct placement tool before any element creation call.
patchQueue.priority_rationale: Elevated to high — the Metromont family category hierarchy (StructuralFraming → StructuralConnection → SpecialtyEquipment → SpecialtyEquipment) makes pre-flight placement info essential for correct tool selection

patchQueue.title: New tool: place_hosted_element
patchQueue.description: A tool for placing Specialty Equipment families hosted inside Structural Connection families, and for placing nested Specialty Equipment inside other Specialty Equipment. Standard place_point_based_element does not handle face-based or host-dependent placement. This tool needs to accept a hostElementId, resolve the host face or work plane, and place the nested family accordingly. Essential for the Metromont consumables workflow (rebar, embeds, hardware nested into connection families).

patchQueue.title: create_sheet assembly sheet support
patchQueue.description: Metromont uses two distinct sheet types: regular sheets for CDs and plate drawings, and Assembly Sheets for shop tickets/fabrication drawings. Current create_sheet creates regular sheets only. Needs an optional isAssemblySheet or sheetType parameter. Assembly sheets in Revit are associated with an Assembly element and have different title block and view placement behavior.

patchQueue.title: query_elements: add parameter-value filtering
patchQueue.description: Current query_elements only filters by category — levelId, bounding box, and familyName filters do not work in practice. Need to add parameterFilters: [{name, value, operator}] support so callers can filter on MANUFACTURE_COMPONENT, ASSEMBLY_COMPONENT, CONSTRUCTION_PRODUCT_HOST, CONTROL_MARK, Assembly Name, BAR_TYPE_* flags etc. This is the foundation of all BOM generation and product-member traversal. Without it, the only way to find assembly members or filter material types is to retrieve thousands of elements and post-filter client-side.
patchQueue.priority_rationale: High — parameter filtering is a prerequisite for BOM tools, assembly traversal, and schedule template work planned for a future session

patchQueue.title: New tool: get_assembly_members
patchQueue.description: Call AssemblyInstance.GetMemberIds() and return member elements with their category, familyName, typeName, and key parameters (CONTROL_MARK, MANUFACTURE_COMPONENT, ASSEMBLY_COMPONENT). Two modes: shallow (direct assembly members only — typically product + connection instance) and deep (recursive — for each connection member enumerate its nested shared SE elements, returning the full 3-level tree: Assembly → Connection → Plate assemblies → Raw materials). Deep mode is required for complete BOM traversal. Without this tool, finding assembly members in a 4858-element project is not feasible.
